keyChanges.title: Ashok: Robotaxi fleet already running early FSD v15 builds — only ~40% of planned improvements, consumer still on v14
keyChanges.description: On the July 22, 2026 Q2 earnings call, Tesla AI chief Ashok Elluswamy confirmed that the currently operating Robotaxi fleet (retrofitted HW4/AI4 Model Ys) is already running early versions of FSD v15 software. He said Tesla targeted seven major improvement tracks over v14 for v15, developed in parallel, and that early fleet builds already contain about 40% of those planned improvements with internal benchmarks hitting their objectives. As work completes, he claimed the car will be 'ridiculously safe and capable.' Critical reality: this is the first official confirmation that any public-road vehicles run v15, ending weeks of 'no public v15 builds' silence — but it is fleet-only, incomplete (~60% of tracks still unfinished), and not a consumer OTA. Production Supervised FSD for owners remains on the v14.3.x branch (v14.3.6 rolling with 2026.20.6.11). Public consumer v15 is still framed as later this year or early next year — the same delayed end-2026/early-2027 window previously cited as the robotaxi-scale architectural blocker. Early v15 on a small unsupervised fleet is validation progress, not the 10B-parameter consumer ship event investors have been waiting for.

positive_signals: Official confirmation from Ashok Elluswamy on Q2 2026 earnings call that Robotaxi fleet runs early FSD v15
Seven major improvement tracks over v14 in development; ~40% already in fleet builds with internal benchmarks meeting objectives
Running on standard HW4/AI4 Model Y robotaxis (plus Project Halo comms) — validates HW4 can host early v15, not Cybercab-only hardware
Corroborated by NotATeslaApp earnings summary + dedicated v15 article citing call segment (~31:58)
negative_signals: Only ~40% of planned v15 improvements — majority of the architectural overhaul still incomplete
No public/consumer v15 OTA; production owners still on Supervised v14.3.x (v14.3.6)
Public consumer v15 timeline unchanged: late 2026 / early 2027 — same delayed window that has blocked large-scale robotaxi expansion guidance
Fleet-only early builds ≠ shipped 10B-parameter consumer architecture Tesla said is required for scale safety
HW3 permanently excluded from unsupervised path and not expected to receive v15

keyChanges.title: FSD v14 Lite goes public for HW3 (2026.20.6.10/.11); HW4 gets point-release v14.3.6 — still Supervised only
keyChanges.description: Tesla restarted and then publicly expanded FSD (Supervised) v14 Lite for HW3/AI3 vehicles with software 2026.20.6.10 (July 20–21), after Ashok Elluswamy said the updated Lite build was 'likely the version that goes to wide release.' NotATeslaApp and TeslaNorth report regular US/Canada HW3 owners beyond early access receiving the OTA; IR shareholder letter confirms v14 Lite delivery began for AI3 customers in the US and South Korea. Official notes: distilled HW4 v14 intelligence into HW3 (RL + offline models), parking/unparking/reversing, Arrival Options, Speed Profiles including SLOTH, optional brake-confirm, Self-Driving app, and streak tracking. Concurrently, 2026.20.6.11 ships FSD Supervised v14.3.6 for HW4 — release notes largely restate the v14.3.5 RL/vision-encoder/MLIR stack with TeslaFi showing ~1.5k cars / ~12% of tracked fleet mid-rollout. Critical reality: this is supervised feature parity and legacy-fleet catch-up, not autonomy progress. Lite is explicitly a distilled student model (slower decision-making than full HW4 v14); HW3 remains permanently capped below unsupervised FSD and is not expected to get v15. Consumer production ceiling is still the v14.3.x branch while robotaxi early-v15 work continues in parallel.

positive_signals: Public HW3 rollout of v14 Lite confirmed by NotATeslaApp, TeslaNorth (US + Canada), and Tesla Q2 IR letter (US + South Korea)
Ashok said updated Lite build is likely the wide-release candidate — rollout advanced beyond early access within ~24 hours
Feature parity gains vs prior HW3: Start from Park, Arrival Options, Speed Profiles, Self-Driving app, streaks, optional brake confirm
HW4 v14.3.6 continuing broader rollout (~11.9% TeslaFi-tracked fleet on 2026.20.6.11)
negative_signals: Still FSD Supervised (SAE L2) only — no unsupervised capability for consumer HW3 or HW4 production software
v14 Lite is a distilled/shrunk model; decision-making slower than full HW4 v14 by design
HW3 permanently excluded from unsupervised FSD and not expected to receive v15 — Lite is effectively the software ceiling until paid hardware upgrades
v14.3.6 is incremental point polish on the same v14.3.x branch covered last week (v14.3.5), not the architectural v15 overhaul
Upcoming Improvements still listed unfixed on v14.3.x notes (expand reasoning beyond destination; pothole avoidance)

keyChanges.title: Q2 IR: 1.48M paid FSD customers (+200k QoQ, +56% YoY); 55% North America delivery attach — supervised software monetizing, unsupervised still blocked
keyChanges.description: Tesla’s Q2 2026 shareholder update and earnings call disclosed active paid FSD customers reached 1.48 million globally (up from 1.28M in Q1 and 0.95M in Q2 2025 — +56% YoY), with record North America attach of over 55% of new deliveries including an FSD subscription at delivery. Mix: ~55% upfront purchases / ~45% subscriptions; Tesla says future monetization growth will skew to subscriptions after removing purchase option in most markets. Cumulative FSD (Supervised) miles approaching 12 billion (consistent with prior-week community 12B milestone). Critical framing: this is strong commercial demand for Supervised L2 software and validates FSD as a demand driver (Musk: buyers want 'FSD with a car attached'), but it is not a software capability milestone. The product customers are buying remains attention-required Supervised FSD on v14.x; the Musk compensation-plan 10M active FSD subscriber target is still ~6.8M away (~15% of goal). Subscription growth can accelerate without shipping unsupervised v15.

positive_signals: Official IR metric: 1.48M active paid FSD customers (upfront + subscriptions, excludes free trials)
Record NA attach: >55% of new deliveries had FSD subscription enabled at delivery
Largest quarterly net-new subscription growth cited (~+200k QoQ); 56% YoY growth from 0.95M
Corroborated across Tesla IR PDF, NotATeslaApp, Teslarati, and TeslaNorth earnings coverage
negative_signals: Product sold is still Supervised L2 — attach rates do not equal unsupervised capability or v15 ship
10M active FSD subscriber compensation milestone remains ~6.8M short (~15% of target)
Tesla removed purchase option / Basic Autopilot to force subscription funnel — growth partly structural, not pure organic capability demand
Cumulative ~12B supervised miles already covered prior week; more data does not complete the remaining ~60% of v15 improvement tracks

categoryUpdate.latestStatus: First official early FSD v15 on Robotaxi fleet (~40% of 7 improvement tracks complete per Ashok). Consumer production still Supervised v14.3.6 (HW4) / v14 Lite (HW3 public rollout). Paid FSD customers 1.48M with 55% NA attach. Public consumer v15 still end-2026/early-2027.
categoryUpdate.nextMilestone: Complete remaining ~60% of v15 improvement tracks; public/consumer FSD v15 OTA (still guided late 2026 or early 2027); broader HW3 v14 Lite wide release internationally
concerns: Early fleet v15 is incomplete (~40% of tracks) — not the full 10B-param architectural ship
Consumer production remains on Supervised v14.3.x while robotaxi scale was previously gated on full v15
HW3 permanently capped at distilled Lite / no unsupervised path without hardware upgrade
v14.3.x still lists core unfixed gaps (reasoning expansion, pothole avoidance)
Subscription/monetization success can mask continued software-architecture delay
